description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison of two multilingual language models—mBERT and XLM-R—across various language families in morphosyntactic probing tasks, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis lists language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents “task count,” ranging from 0 to 40, indicating the number of probing tasks evaluated per language family. Each language family has three stacked bars representing outcomes: “better” for mBERT (light blue), “better” for XLM-R (dark blue), and “same” (light green), as defined in the legend. For example, in IE-Slavic, XLM-R outperforms mBERT in nearly 40 tasks, while mBERT performs better in about 12 tasks, and they perform equally in around 28 tasks. In contrast, for IE-Indic, both models show minimal advantage over each other, with most tasks yielding “same” results. The chart reveals that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT across most language families, particularly in IE-Slavic and Uralic, while mBERT shows a slight edge only in IE-Slavic and IE-Romance. The “same” category is consistently present across all families, indicating substantial overlap in model performance. No bars are sorted by height, and no visual emphasis (e.g., shading or annotations) is applied beyond the color-coded legend.
